scope: Steam-centered indie market signals and official reference-game evidence; not a genre popularity ranking or sales forecast.
methodology: Release counts and 1,000-review thresholds come from How To Market A Game analyses using VG Insights data and Steam tags. They are analyst classifications, not Valve sales reports.
Submitted reviews, concurrent players, wishlists and cumulative players are different metrics and are not added together or ranked against each other.
Review counts and concurrent-player positions are snapshots checked on 2026-10-17 and can change after publication.
Players must not be relabeled as copies sold. Free-game concurrent players do not directly measure paid demand or active attention.
GameplayBorrow is a design interpretation. The cited result does not prove that one mechanic caused a reference game's success.

sources.publisher: How To Market A Game, using VG Insights data
sources.caveat: A hit is defined by the article as at least 1,000 reviews by the snapshot. Tags can overlap and this is not confirmed revenue or copies sold.

sources.publisher: How To Market A Game, using VG Insights data
sources.caveat: The rise of hands-on first-person job simulators is the author's interpretation of tagged releases, not an official industry statistic.
The developer announcement says players, not copies sold, and does not publish a detailed counting methodology. Review values are a checked-date snapshot.
Submitted English reviews are not official sales or total player counts.
The official one-million figure is prelaunch wishlists, not copies sold. Reviews are a checked-date snapshot.
A single live snapshot of a free desktop idle game. It does not establish paid demand, sustained rank or active attention.
Players across Steam, Xbox and PlayStation, including subscription access, are not copies sold. This is an outlier-scale reference, not a realistic small-team production comparison.
A niche review signal, not an official sales count. The separate 30,000 crowdfunding figure is not used because it was a Modian goal amount, not copies sold.
